messages:
alex: quick question — I noticed the embeddings endpoint is returning a single vector when I POST a lone string, but a list when I pass an array. Spec says always list. Did we ship a change?

maria: good catch. Which model + example payload?

alex: model: text-embed-redwood-3072, payload: {
  "input": "short doc"
} -> server returns [3072 numbers] (no outer list). If I send {
  "input": ["short doc"]
} it returns [[3072 numbers]].

devon: that was a canary tweak from runtime yesterday — we temporarily allowed scalar->vector auto-unpack for single string to keep old mobile SDKs happy. It was meant to be behind a flag but leak happened.

ryan: ugh, that breaks parity for typed clients expecting list-of-vectors. We should revert or add explicit Content-Type header behavior.

devon: agreed. Plan: revert the unpacking within 1 hr, and add an explicit compatibility header X-Embed-Compat: legacy to enable old behavior. New default will always return an array-of-vectors.

alex: thanks. Also noticed doc around truncation is vague. Current behavior?

maria: current runtime truncation rules (deployed):

- Accepts input as either a single string or an array of strings or array of objects {"id","text"}.
- Max batch size: 1024 items per request.
- Max total payload: 8MB (post-JSON bytes) per request.
- Per-input truncation: first limit is 64k characters, then tokenized with our byte-pair tokenizer and clipped to 4096 tokens for embedding input.
- If an object has an "id", response preserves order and returns [{"id":..., "embedding": [...]}, ...]. Without ids we return [ [...], ... ].

ryan: will that change vector shape? model is 3072 dims, right?

maria: correct — text-embed-redwood-3072 returns 3072-d vectors. We also surface model profile in /models endpoint.

alex: can you paste a sample response formats? small ones for the doc.

maria: sure:

Request A (single string):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "input": "short doc"
}
```
Response (new default):
```
{
  "data": [
    {"embedding": [0.001, -0.23, ... 3072 floats ...]}
  ],
  "model": "text-embed-redwood-3072"
}
```

Request B (array of objects with ids):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "input": [
    {"id": "docA", "text": "first"},
    {"id": "docB", "text": "second"}
  ]
}
```
Response:
```
{
  "data": [
    {"id":"docA","embedding": [...]},
    {"id":"docB","embedding": [...]}
  ],
  "model": "text-embed-redwood-3072"
}
```

devon: note: when payload is near 8MB we start rejecting with 413 and a structured error: {"error":{"type":"payload_too_large","message":"total request exceeds 8MB"}}. Also batch ordering preserved except when user omits ids.

alex: perfect. A couple follow ups: update openapi docs, and add a migration note for SDK owners. Can we add a deprecation header for one week before revert, so clients see change?

devon: i'll push a canary revert + header: X-Embed-Behavior: array-by-default (after 1h), and for one week we'll emit X-Embed-Announcement: will-enforce-array. ci-bot will post a deploy message.

ci-bot: deploy queued: runtime/embed-unpack-revert (canary) -> started. CI link: https://ci.redwood/run/3210 :rocket:

maria: i'll update docs PR with truncation + batching rules and add example responses. tagging @eng-platform for rollout notes.

ryan: thanks team. i'll audit SDKs for any deserialization logic that expects scalar vector and open PRs as needed.

alex: resolving once canary confirmed. :thumbsup:
